project.title: Hotel Ops Copilot: Governed Multi-Agent Hotel Operations on IBM Db2
project.short_description: A LangGraph multi-agent copilot for hotel duty managers. Agents analyse occupancy and revenue with text-to-SQL, mine guest reviews with Db2 vector search, and propose pricing, upgrade and maintenance actions. A human approves each action, Db2 stored procedures enforce the guardrails, and system-period temporal tables make every change auditable and reversible.
project.category: Agentic AI / Text-to-SQL / Vector Search / Governance

members.name: Clark Fernandes
members.role: Solo developer: Db2 design, agents, UI

ibm_db2.connector: ibm_db (native Python driver) wrapped as LangChain tools, plus IBM langchain-db2 (DB2VS vector store) via ibm_db_dbi
features_used: VECTOR(384, FLOAT32) columns + VECTOR_DISTANCE cosine search over sentence-level chunks
In-database complaint classification: VALUES anchor vectors CROSS JOIN sentence vectors, ROW_NUMBER() OVER, GROUP BY GROUPING SETS
Transactional dry run of agent actions: real stored procedure inside a unit of work, diff, ROLLBACK
System-period temporal tables (FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF / FROM..TO) for audit, a trigger-free change feed and one-click rollback
SQL PL stored procedures enforcing business guardrails
Bitemporal table PROMOTIONS: BUSINESS_TIME + SYSTEM_TIME, BUSINESS_TIME WITHOUT OVERLAPS key, UPDATE ... FOR PORTION OF BUSINESS_TIME, and FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF ... FOR BUSINESS_TIME AS OF queries
Materialized query table MQT_DAILY_KPIS (REFRESH DEFERRED, ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION) for KPI history
Row and Column Access Control: column masks for PII and a row permission enforcing AI-processing consent

Hotel-chain property isolation: PROPERTY_ID on 15 tables with composite foreign keys, and RCAC row permissions (history tables and the MQT included) against a manager-only AGENT_SCOPE table, so each AI identity sees and acts on its own hotel only
Roles and least-privilege GRANTs for the AI agent identity
JSON_VALUE and a JSON_EXISTS check constraint on action payloads
Analytic views, GROUP BY ROLLUP, ROW_NUMBER() OVER, recursive CTE calendar
Catalog COMMENTs (SYSCAT) as the semantic layer for text-to-SQL; LISTAGG over SYSCAT.COLUMNS gives the agents exact column lists

Agent run and step audit trail stored in Db2, tamper-evident via a SHA-256 hash chain (trigger + HASH + LAG verification), plus an external anchor of the chain head that catches a fully rebuilt ledger
Earned autonomy: AUTONOMY_POLICY temporal table; the decision is made inside SP_PROPOSE_ACTION
EXPLAIN PLAN cost guard on agent-written SQL (SYSTOOLS explain tables)

Label-based access control (LBAC): GUEST_NOTES rows carry DB2SECURITYLABEL values (PUBLIC/INTERNAL/RESTRICTED) under a security policy with DB2LBACRULES; the agent holds an INTERNAL read label; labels are managed by a separate SECADM; combined with an RCAC consent permission on the same table
Adaptive row compression (COMPRESS YES ADAPTIVE) on reservations, rates, their history tables and the agent audit steps
Db2 workload management: the AI login runs in its own WORKLOAD with THRESHOLDs on estimated cost, rows returned and run time (STOP EXECUTION), and a THRESHOLD VIOLATIONS event monitor logs every stop
Policy knowledge base in Db2 via IBM langchain-db2 DB2VS
Red-team scoreboard: 24/24 attacks blocked, mostly by Db2 privileges, RCAC and SQL PL guardrails
python src/verify.py: 32 live checks of every claim against Db2 (no LLM key); guardrail fuzzing with 10,000 random proposals vs an independent oracle (10,000/10,000 agree)

ai_models: Google Gemini 3.5 Flash with a quota-aware fallback chain (configurable: watsonx.ai, OpenAI, Ollama)
